title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 221 (Freezing of assets of company on inquiry and investigation)

content.overview: Section 221 empowers the Tribunal, on a reference by the Central Government or by any person interested or on an application by the Registrar or inspector during inquiry or investigation, to order that any transfer, removal or disposal of funds, assets or properties of the company shall not take place, or that any transfer of securities shall not take place, during such period not exceeding three years as may be specified, if the Tribunal is satisfied that removal, transfer or disposal is likely to take place which may prejudicially affect the interests of the company or its shareholders or creditors or the public interest. The order is an interim preservation measure and is not a finding of fraud.
content.glance: During inquiry/investigation: Tribunal may freeze company assets or securities transfers for up to three years on reference/application; interim preservation; not a finding of fraud.
content.study: Where it appears to the Tribunal, on a reference made to it by the Central Government or by any person interested or on an application made by the Registrar or inspector under this Chapter, that removal, transfer or disposal of funds, assets or properties of the company is likely to take place in a manner prejudicial to the interests of the company or its shareholders or creditors or in public interest, the Tribunal may by order direct that such transfer, removal or disposal shall not take place during such period not exceeding three years as may be specified, or that any transfer of securities shall not take effect. Current-law framing: confirm ongoing inquiry or investigation; standing of the applicant (CG, interested person, Registrar or inspector); Tribunal satisfaction that prejudicial removal/transfer is likely; order freezing assets or securities transfers for a period not exceeding three years.

sections.heading: Standing
sections.body: Reference by Central Government or any person interested, or application by Registrar or inspector, during inquiry or investigation.

sections.heading: Ground
sections.body: Tribunal satisfied that removal, transfer or disposal of funds, assets or properties is likely in a manner prejudicial to the company, shareholders, creditors or public interest.

sections.heading: Order
sections.body: Freeze on transfer/removal/disposal of assets, or on transfer of securities, for a period not exceeding three years.

sections.heading: Nature
sections.body: Interim preservation order; not a finding of fraud or final adjudication on merits.

provisions.title: Freezing of assets of company on inquiry and investigation

examples.title: Asset freeze during investigation
examples.body: During a s. 210 investigation the Registrar applies to the Tribunal alleging that company funds are about to be transferred abroad. The Tribunal, satisfied of likely prejudice, may order a freeze under s. 221 for a period not exceeding three years.

examples.title: Not a fraud finding
examples.body: A freeze order under s. 221 is passed. That does not itself establish that the company or its officers committed fraud; it is a preservation measure pending inquiry or investigation.

hypotheticals.question: Can the Tribunal freeze assets under s. 221 indefinitely?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 221 limits the period of the order to not exceeding three years as may be specified in the order.

distinctions.title: Freezing of assets (s. 221) vs restrictions upon securities (s. 222)
distinctions.left: Freeze on transfer/removal/disposal of company funds, assets or properties, or on securities transfers
distinctions.right: Restrictions on transfer or exercise of rights attached to securities in connection with investigation

misconceptions.trap: A s. 221 freeze is a permanent confiscation of company assets.
misconceptions.correction: Section 221 authorises a time-limited (not exceeding three years) interim order restraining transfer, removal or disposal. It is preservation, not confiscation.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 221 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm inquiry/investigation and standing. II. Test likely prejudice. III. Apply freeze within three-year limit. IV. Note interim nature. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Inquiry status; prejudice facts; freeze sought; precise relief.

examTips: Standing: CG, interested person, Registrar, inspector.
